text.en: You eat a roti at lunch. By evening it is gone, but it has become energy and part of your body. How? Animals use food through digestion, breathing, circulation and excretion.

Animals cannot make their own food. They get nutrients by eating plants or other animals. Digestion is breaking food into small simple substances the body can absorb. In humans it starts in the mouth, where teeth chew and saliva begins digesting starch. Food passes through the food pipe to the stomach, where acids and juices work, then to the small intestine, where most digestion and absorption happen. The large intestine takes in water and the rest leaves as waste.
Respiration is releasing energy from food using oxygen. We breathe in air with oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide. The lungs exchange gases. Fish use gills and insects use tiny tubes.
The heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of the body. Blood carries food and oxygen to cells and takes away waste. Red blood cells carry oxygen. Plasma carries food. White blood cells fight germs.
Excretion is removing waste from the body. The kidneys filter blood and make urine. Lungs remove carbon dioxide and the skin removes sweat.
